<reason>A won by making the word "mainly" the decision rule and then holding B to it. Two of A's moves did real damage: (1) the staggered-closing turn, showing that B's signature "last-call stampede" harm is best solved by licensing sequencing — i.e., a venue restriction — which concedes A's instrument; and (2) the dose-asymmetry argument, that pure displacement cannot explain why lengthening trading hours raises harm, only relocating it back. B's reply to that ("counted corridor incidents rise because more people remain on a dense street") was fairly characterized by A as an admission rather than a measurement artefact. Most decisively, A's pressure question asked B to name any case where transit and street presence alone made nightlife measurably safer; B answered "I will not pretend that is the motion," which reads as evasion of exactly the burden the proposition imposes, and it compounded B's earlier concession that a bus "is not meant to outperform a lockout at stopping bar fights." A also neutralized the strandedness core by absorbing it: A funds the last train and lighting, but releases crowds into a network the city already owns, so B's distinctive contribution shrinks to the marginal late-shift worker. B's best live threads — displacement to cars and unlicensed rooms, and the late kitchen staff who miss the ordinary timetable — survived but were partly answered (low-density settings lack the corridor's ingredients; 3 a.m. leavers drive drunker). B argued with real clarity and a memorable frame, but never established why the exit should be the *primary* reliance rather than the complement A already grants, which is the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's pressure question demanding a case where late transit and street teams alone reduced night-time assaults, met by B's "I will not pretend that is the motion" — an evasion A then converted, alongside B's earlier "a bus is not meant to outperform a lockout," into the claim that B's own instrument cannot bear the word "mainly."</best_rebuttal>
